plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction) with 3 bidders. In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so there's no incentive to shade my bid down, and bidding higher than my value risks negative profit. Therefore, I should bid exactly my value of $25.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding my true value ensures I only win when it's profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. Bidding higher risks winning at a loss; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With value $17, I'll bid exactly $17.

This holds because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so bidding your true value maximizes expected profit - if you bid higher, you risk winning at a price above your value; if you bid lower, you risk losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $39, I should bid exactly $39.
